editorial:
Imagine you are at the top of your game, crushing it at work in New York City, and suddenly your whole world flips upside down. C. Wiatt. She is a high-powered executive who thinks she has everything figured out until a surprise baby lands in her lap. You will love how the movie balances the stress of corporate life with the chaos of diaper changes. It is a lighthearted ride that feels like a cozy hug, showing you the struggle of a woman trying to prove she can handle a career and motherhood at the same time without losing her mind.

Diane Keaton is absolutely great here, bringing a quirky energy that keeps the story moving fast. While some of the plot twists feel a bit predictable, the charm makes up for it. If you want a feel-good story about independence, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: After being pushed out of her firm, J.C. starts her own successful business from home while raising Elizabeth. She proves that she does not need a big boss to be a winner. In the end, she finds a new romantic interest who actually supports her as a mother. She manages to balance her professional success and her love for the baby, showing everyone that you can define success on your own terms.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic 80s comedies and stories about female empowerment.
